clue.text: Welsh pop singer makes a packet

parts.note: a rapper is a performer of rap, a kind of pop music

explanation.surface: A Welsh pop star earns a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a packet' reads as earning a lot of money; 'makes' is only a link, and 'packet' is the parcel sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is the paper or film that encloses goods, much like a packet holding them.

clue.text: Dockland song said to cause conflict

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and only their sound counts

parts.note: a wharf is a quay in a dockland and an air is a song

explanation.surface: A dockside ditty is claimed to start a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed hostilities between nations, a state of war.

clue.text: Current indicator

parts.note: looks like a sign of present trends but means a meter for electric flow

explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter measures electric flow in amperes, so it shows how much is passing.

clue.text: Advance made by head of church house

definitions.meaning: the superior of a monastery or religious community

explanation.surface: Promotion awarded by the leader of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means earlier or in advance; as a noun it is the monk ranking just below an abbot.

clue.text: Make its curate become countrified

indicators.note: make tells you to construct something new from the letters of its curate

explanation.surface: A demand that a clergyman turn rustic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like part of the definition 'make ... countrified'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to go and live in the country, adopting rural ways.

clue.text: Fellow takes second to enhance his appearance

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A man takes a moment to make himself look better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a moment of time; here it is the second of two, the latter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that flatter someone show them in a more becoming light.

clue.text: In favour of church using coercion…

parts.note: for means supporting, in favour of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A supporter of the church who resorts to pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Force is compulsion or constraint applied to make someone act.

clue.text: …if servers remove royal tabs

indicators.note: remove here means shift around, so the letters of royal tabs are moved

explanation.surface: Waiters might take away the regal bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servers' suggests waiters; it means those who assist a priest at the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Altar boys assist the priest during Mass, serving at the altar.

clue.text: Set one's sights on being educated

definitions.meaning: aimed a gun or camera at

explanation.surface: Aiming at a target while being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun trained on a target is aimed at it; a person trained has been instructed or coached.

clue.text: What this snake did when agitated?

definitions.meaning: a rattlesnake shakes its tail to make a noise

explanation.surface: Wondering what a snake did when it was stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake shakes its tail rattle; colloquially someone shaken or flustered is unnerved.

clue.text: Stays to get left-overs

definitions.meaning: stays put, continues to be there
what is left behind after the rest is gone

explanation.surface: Someone stays behind to collect the scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to linger on, a verb sense; as a plural noun the word means residue or what survives.

clue.text: Withdraw remarks about political pamphlet

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning
a tract is a short polemical pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone takes back comments made concerning a party leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay what one said earlier is to take back or recant one's words.

clue.text: Death or the world to come

definitions.meaning: cryptically, what comes after one's life ends
existence beyond the grave, heaven or hereafter

explanation.surface: A choice between dying and the hereafter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AFTER LIFE, the phrase means what follows living, which is death.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereafter is believed to follow mortal existence, and read in two words it is simply what follows living.

clue.text: Learn about the kidneys

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning relating to the kidneys

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of learn are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to study the kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', which would make the definition; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the medical adjective for anything to do with these organs, as in renal failure.

clue.text: Always first? That's odd!

indicators.note: first places the always piece at the front, ahead of the next one

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Being permanently in the lead seems strange to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of E'ER and the dots of I.E. are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is uncanny or weird, strange in an unsettling way.

clue.text: Damaged retina, yes, causes visual impairment

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of retina and yes are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An injured retina, it is confirmed, leads to poor vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness of the eyes from overuse, blurring or weakening sight.

clue.text: Vamoosed after second bad work placement

indicators.note: the letters are worked over and placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ran off after a second disastrous stint of work experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work placement' looks like an internship; it signals that SECOND BAD is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamoose is slang for to leave hurriedly, the same as fleeing secretly.

clue.text: She hangs her stocking on it

definitions.text: She hangs her stocking on it

parts.words: She hangs her stocking on it
parts.note: sounds like a Christmas hook or mantelpiece, but is the garter strap holding up hosiery

explanation.walkthrough: In British English these are the straps on a woman's garter belt, not trouser braces.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is an elastic strap clipped to the top of a stocking to hold it up; in American usage a garter.

clue.text: Settled by male head showing flexibility

parts.note: a bird lit on a branch, meaning settled
he is the male pronoun
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours or Inverness place names

explanation.surface: A man settled down and showed he could bend.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS (a headland or promontory) appears in British place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Litheness is suppleness, the quality of bending easily.

clue.text: Barge with comparatively little cargo

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed boat used for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A barge carrying less than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat boat for ferrying goods to and from ships; as a comparative adjective it means less heavy.

clue.text: Labour and Tory rebels initially need help

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letters of Tory and rebels

parts.note: avail means help or benefit, as in to no avail

explanation.surface: Both main parties have rebels who need assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party beside 'Tory'; it is toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil or hard work, also the pains of childbirth.

clue.text: Drink to HM? Fantastic!

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A toast to the monarch, cheered enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink to HM' reads as raising a glass to the sovereign; 'to' just links SUP and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Heads accommodate Irish freebooters

indicators.note: accommodate means the heads word gives room to the Irish piece inside it

parts.note: pates are heads, especially bald tops of heads

explanation.surface: Leaders take in Irish buccaneers.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebooters are plunderers, sea robbers who raid ships.

clue.text: Regret using sappers' code

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers, are the RE
Morse is the dot-and-dash telegraph code

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to be using military signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep contrition or guilt for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Work hard to make illicit profit

definitions.meaning: money gained by corruption or bribery

explanation.surface: Advice to toil so as to make crooked money.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to toil, an informal British sense; the noun means bribery and corrupt gain in politics.

clue.text: Realm most affected by violent disorder

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of realm most are changed around

explanation.surface: A kingdom is hit hardest by rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violent disorder' looks like a riot; it is a whirlpool or turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, and figuratively any scene of turbulent confusion.

clue.text: Comes across lots of hunters

definitions.meaning: gatherings of riders and hounds for a hunt

explanation.surface: Someone encounters a crowd of huntsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet is to encounter; a meet is a British fox-hunting assembly, so several are groups of huntsmen.

clue.text: Cut corners to give snow-shoe to member

parts.note: a ski is a runner worn for travelling over snow
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Economising by giving an MP some winter footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise stingily, doing a job with too little effort or material.

clue.text: You can serve it with beverage and gateau

parts.note: tea is a common beverage
a gateau is a rich cake

explanation.surface: A suggestion for what to put out alongside drinks and dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A teacake is a British toasted sweet bun with currants, served buttered.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttered bun with currants is something offered to guests at tea, so it is a thing one serves.

clue.text: Crack found in the Austrian boat

indicators.note: found in says the crack piece sits within the Austrian article

parts.note: der is German for the, the language of Austria
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A fissure is discovered in an Austrian vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing vessel that uses drift nets.

clue.text: Reportedly regret heather's injunctions

indicators.note: reportedly says the regret and heather pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: rue means regret and ling is heather, so rue ling's

explanation.surface: Someone is said to lament a heath plant's legal orders.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is a heather common on British moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulings are official decisions or orders handed down, like court directives.

clue.text: Smart answer from east German in mellow housing

indicators.note: housing means the mellow word holds the German piece inside it

parts.note: ripe fruit or cheese is mature, mellow
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: A clever reply comes from an East German living in a laid-back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the old GDR; it is just the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, witty retort.
